title: Orrin’s seasons, with a sort and a fork (a CI fixture)
dek: An invented planet, a chain to put in order and two paths to choose between (a CI fixture).

blocks.text: Orrin leans by 31 degrees, and the lean points the same way all year. So why does it have seasons at all?

stops.prompt: What makes a season on Orrin?
stops.explain: The lean changes how steeply sunlight strikes each half through the year.
stops.twist: Distance is the natural first guess. On Orrin it hardly changes, so it cannot be the cause.

blocks.text: Here is the chain, shuffled. Put the causes in the order they happen, from the lean to the warming of the north.

interactive.explain: The lean sets the angle of the light, the angle sets how long and how strong the days are, and that warms the north.

blocks.text: A low sun spreads the same light over more ground, so each patch gets less.

stops.simple: A low sun spreads light thin.

guide.line: Same sunshine, more ground: that is all a low sun is.

blocks.text: Orrin has two halves, and you can follow either one through the year. Choose what to read next.

stops.simple: Follow one half through the year.

interactive.prompt: Which half do you want to follow?

branches.label: The north
branches.text: The north warms while its lean points toward Vael, and its days run long.

branches.label: The south
branches.text: The south cools in those same months, because its lean points away and the light is low.

stops.prompt: Which place changes least across the year?
stops.explain: Near the equator the noon sun stays high in every season.
stops.twist: The poles feel the biggest swing, so it is easy to look for the calm elsewhere.

blocks.text: Whichever path you took, the two meet here: the lean is fixed, and the light does the rest.

guide.line: Fixed lean, moving light. See you at the end.

stops.prompt: If Orrin did not lean at all, what would happen to its seasons?
stops.explain: Without a lean, the sun would stand at the same height all year, so the seasons would fade.
stops.twist: It is tempting to think the lean only adds a little. It is the whole cause.

asides.title: Where this stops
asides.text: Orrin is invented for this fixture, and a real planet has more going on than one chain of causes.

askSuggestions: What would change if the numbers were different?
Where does this picture stop being true?
